name: Lycabettus Loft
summary: The most contemporary space in the house: a glass-fronted loft looking straight at Lycabettus.
description: Set back behind the neoclassical cornice, under the original roof timbers. Microcement floors, a low platform bed, a walk-in rain shower and full-height glass doors that open onto a 20 m² terrace facing Lycabettus.

name: Strefi Suite
summary: Pared-back and olive-toned, with a balcony that leans into the pines of Strefi Hill.
description: Behind the tall original balcony doors: a calm suite of olive microcement, oak and linen. A built-in reading nook doubles as a day bed for a third guest, and the iron balcony looks straight into the trees across the street.
photoCaption: The steps up to Strefi Hill
original: Tall balcony doors and iron railing

name: Neapoli Studio
summary: A compact, clever studio for couples who plan to spend their days out exploring.
description: The original mosaic floor meets a single wall of built-in oak joinery that hides the kitchenette, wardrobe and a fold-down desk. Bright, uncluttered and quietly clever, with a tall window over Koumarianou Street.

name: Exarchia Family Apartment
summary: The old reception rooms, opened up into one generous space for families and friends.
description: We joined the formal rooms of the old house into a single open-plan living space with a full kitchen and a 2.4 m oak dining table, under the original ceiling roses. Two separate bedrooms; a travel cot and high chair are available on request.

name: Courtyard Garden Apartment
summary: Stone walls, steel and glass, opening onto the courtyard and its old lemon tree.
description: Exposed stone from the original foundations, a step-free layout and steel-framed glass doors onto the shared courtyard, where the lemon tree planted by the first owners still bears fruit every winter.

name: The Neoclassical
summary: Where the old house and the new are most in dialogue.
description: The 3.6 m ceilings, plaster mouldings and restored wooden shutters of the original piano nobile, furnished with pieces by contemporary Greek designers and work by young Athenian artists. The house at its most dramatic.
